criteria.criterion: Central passenger service between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood commenced by December 2018
required_elements: Crossrail/Elizabeth line central passenger service commenced
service covered the central section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood
criteria.promise_scope: Crossrail promised that Crossrail services would commence in December 2018 in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood in London; beneficiaries are intended passengers using that central section, though no narrower passenger group is specified.
criteria.observed_scope: Evidence shows the Elizabeth line central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood was operating for passengers by its opening day in May 2022; the cited evidence does not show commencement by December 2018, and one source states the opening decision had already shifted to Autumn 2019 in August 2018.
criteria.timing_requirement: By December 2018 (original promise: “December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood”).
criteria.explanation: c1 documents the original undertaking: service commencement in December 2018 on the central section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood. c2 directly contradicts delivery by that date, stating that on 29 August 2018 the Crossrail Ltd Board decided to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 instead. c3 and c4 then show the service eventually did open and operate between Paddington and Abbey Wood, with opening-day journeys reported in 2022, but these later results confirm that commencement was after December 2018, not by it.

trace.label: REFUTED
trace.verdict: The original promise is documented, but the cited evidence refutes that the central Paddington-to-Abbey Wood passenger service opened by December 2018. Crossrail originally said services would commence in December 2018, then officially shifted the opening to Autumn 2019, and the cited operating evidence is from the actual 2022 opening.
trace.reasoning:
Requested scope: Did London's Elizabeth line open its central passenger service from Paddington to Abbey Wood by the originally planned December 2018 date?

The question asks about actual opening by the originally planned December 2018 date, not merely whether that date was announced. The original scope is a London central-section passenger service between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood. c1 establishes that promise. c2 is direct evidence incompatible with delivery by December 2018 because it says the board decided on 29 August 2018 to open that same central section in Autumn 2019. c3 and c4 corroborate that the service eventually operated between Paddington and Abbey Wood, but only later. Therefore the promised December 2018 commencement did not occur.

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood”
https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/annual-update-on-crossrail-2017

c2: “The Crossrail Ltd Board took the decision to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 on 29 August 2018.”
https://tfl.gov.uk/corporate/transparency/freedom-of-information/foi-request-detail?referenceId=FOI-1470-1819

c3: “The Elizabeth line will operate 12 trains per hour between Paddington and Abbey Wood from Monday to Saturday 06:30 to 23:00.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-elizabeth-line-to-open-on-24-may-2022

c4: “The celebratory response to the opening saw around 260,000 journeys made on the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood across its opening day, clearly showing its popularity.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-celebrations-as-transformational-elizabeth-line-begins-operations

refutation.quote: The Crossrail Ltd Board took the decision to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 on 29 August 2018.
The celebratory response to the opening saw around 260,000 journeys made on the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood across its opening day, clearly showing its popularity.
